channel.title: Wyoming Public Media - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Wyoming Public Media (wyomingpublicmedia.org)

item.title: Senate reverts largely to governor’s budget proposal while House still deliberating cuts
item.description: The Wyoming House and Senate are arriving at markedly different versions of the budget bill. The Senate finished second reading with a bill that largely restores the governor’s original funding proposal, while the House is still debating its first round of amendments as of publication time.

item.title: Medical experts offer tips for maintaining good heart health
item.description: February is American Heart Month and health experts are putting a spotlight on cardiovascular diseases and the tools available to all Wyomingites to help save lives. Heart disease is the leading cause of death in Wyoming and high blood pressure is one of the leading precursors of life-changing events like heart attack or stroke.

item.title: Lawmakers want to convert natural gas to more marketable products like hydrogen
item.description: Some West Coast states have blocked Wyoming’s fossil fuel exports. But lawmakers are trying to get around that with new legislation.

item.title: Wyoming Debrief February 19, 2026
item.description: Today’s trivia question: What is Wyoming’s largest agricultural commodity? Send us your answer to WyomingPublicRadio@gmail.com or by message on Instagram or Facebook. We’ll give a shout out to the first person to submit the correct answer.

item.title: Elder Statesman of Aviation #572: W. Dillard “Pic” Walker Papers
item.description: W. Dillard “Pic” Walker was named an “Elder Statesman of Aviation” by the National Aeronautic Association in 1992. The award capped a 40-year career as a pilot and aviation pioneer.

item.title: Feds exclude untested nuclear reactors from environmental review
item.description: The Trump administration has eliminated a critical review step for experimental nuclear reactors. The U.S. Department of Energy has posted a notice to the Federal Register that it is excluding advanced nuclear reactors from review under the National Environmental Policy Act. The agency is accepting public comments on the new exclusion through March 4.

item.title: Senate moves bill that would cement Cheyenne as the new PRCA headquarters
item.description: Cheyenne is one step closer to becoming the Professional Rodeo Cowboys Association's headquarters. A bill that would provide $15 million to help move the PRCA from Colorado Springs has passed its second reading in the Senate.

item.title: House adopts steep cuts to proposed budget. Senate delays final reading
item.description: Wyoming Business Council funding. Pay raises for correctional officers. The opportunity for more suicide prevention education in schools. All were budget bill amendments that members of the Wyoming House killed this week.

item.title: Senate adds WPM funding back to state budget as House keeps it out
item.description: As they prepare to give the state budget a final look, Wyoming’s two chambers will begin with radically different versions of what was once an identical bill.
